Draw the matrix of a janusplot fit

Source: R/plot.R
plot.janusplot_fit.Rd

Draws the asymmetric matrix of a janusplot_fit() object: one cell per directed pair, the fitted curve with its band over the raw points, the variable names along the top and left borders. Nothing is refitted; every number on the plot is in the object.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'janusplot_fit'
plot(
  x,
  colour_by = c("nonlinearity", "asymmetry", "pearson", "spearman", "kendall",
    "deviance_gap", "none"),
  background_by = c("pearson", "spearman", "kendall", "none"),
  annotations = NULL,
  order = c("original", "hclust", "alphabetical"),
  display = c("fit", "d1", "d2"),
  group = NULL,
  focus_by = NA_character_,
  focus_threshold = "q90",
  axes = c("original", "standardised", "centred", "rank"),
  style = janusplot_style(),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A janusplot_fit object.

colour_by

The quantity painted on each cell: "nonlinearity" (the default; EDF minus 1 of the cell's smooth, sequential from 0), "asymmetry" (the pair's index A in [0, 1], the same in both cells), "pearson", "spearman" or "kendall" (the pair's correlation on a diverging scale over [-1, 1]), "deviance_gap" (deviance explained by the smooth minus the straight line's) or "none".

background_by

The correlation that tints each cell's background: "pearson", "spearman", "kendall", or "none" for no background. Left unset, it is "pearson" for a marginal fit and "none" for a fit with adjust, whose curves are adjusted while the correlations are marginal; set it to show the marginal correlation behind adjusted curves. Independent of colour_by. It cannot be combined with janusplot_style(colour_channel = "fill"), which paints the same area.

annotations

Character vector, a subset of c("A", "edf", "signif", "code", "shape", "k_warn", "n", "r", "formula"), written in the strip of every cell (or in its corners under janusplot_style(annotation_position = "corners")): the asymmetry index, the EDF, the significance glyph of the smooth F-test (*** p < .001, ** p < .01, * p < .05, . p < .1, from the adjusted p-value when the fit has p_adjust other than "none"), the two-letter shape code, the shape glyph, a warning sign on cells flagged by the k-check or capped at the distinct predictor count, the rows used, the background_by correlation of the pair (Pearson when background_by = "none"), printed "r -0.03" ("marginal r -0.03" for a fit with adjust), and the cell's formula, printed Temp ~ Ozone. NULL (the default) picks by matrix size: c("A", "signif") up to twelve variables, "signif" from thirteen, where 5-point strips of neighbouring cells would touch; character() writes none.

order

Order of the variables in the matrix: "original" (the default, the order of x$vars), "hclust" (hierarchical clustering of absolute Pearson correlations) or "alphabetical". Drawing only; the fit is unchanged.

display

What every off-diagonal cell shows: "fit" (the default), "d1" (the first derivative of the smooth, whose zero crossings are turning points) or "d2" (the second derivative, whose zero crossings are inflections). A derivative view needs the fit to carry that order in x$settings$derivatives.

group

Name of a factor, character or logical column of x$data whose levels colour the raw points, with one legend below the matrix, or NULL (the default). Drawing only; the column never enters the model. The column must exist in x$data and have at most style$group_max_levels levels.

focus_by

NA (the default, no filter) or one of "asymmetry", "edf", "non_linearity" (EDF minus 1) and "k_flag". Cells whose metric falls below focus_threshold are washed in grey at style$focus_dim_alpha; the matrix keeps its shape. A visual filter only; the fit and its table are unchanged.

focus_threshold

A quantile string, "q90" by default (taken over the off-diagonal cells), or a single numeric cutoff. Ignored when focus_by is NA.

axes

Scale of the drawn axes: "original" (the default), "standardised" ((x - mean) / sd per variable, border label "var (z)"), "centred" (x - mean, label "var (centred)") or "rank" (empirical rank, label "rank(var)"). Drawing only; the same transform is applied to the points, the curve and the band.

style

A janusplot_style() object holding every appearance setting.

...

Must be empty. An unknown name is an error, so a misspelt style knob cannot pass silently.

Value

A patchwork object, which is a ggplot: the matrix with its border labels and corner key, the colour bar when colour_by is not "none", the background colour bar when background_by is not "none", the group legend when group is given, the shape-categories legend when style$show_shape_legend is TRUE, or "auto" and annotations include "code", a title naming the displayed quantity and the glossary caption when style$show_glossary is TRUE.

Details

Every off-diagonal cell [r, c] shows vars[r] ~ s(vars[c]): the variable named left of the row is the response on the vertical axis and the variable named above the column is the predictor on the horizontal axis, as in graphics::pairs(). Cells [r, c] and [c, r] are the two directions of one pair and differ by design. A key in the top-left corner shows the convention with the first two variables (style$show_key).

The colour_by value is painted on the border, a corner tile or the whole cell per style$colour_channel, with one colour bar per matrix. The background_by correlation tints the panel behind the points, band and curve: white at zero and style$background_strength of the way to the negative or positive end of style$background_palette at minus or plus one, with its own colour bar over [-1, 1]. A strip above each cell carries the annotations; the asymmetry index belongs to the pair and is written once, above the cell in the upper triangle. The diagonal shows the kernel density of each variable with a rug of its values, and with group one density per level, scaled by the level's share of the rows so the coloured curves sum to the grey pooled density (style$diagonal).

The default sizes are set for a figure one page wide (170 mm). At one journal column (85 mm), draw at most four variables with janusplot_style(text_size = 6, show_shape_legend = FALSE, show_glossary = FALSE).

The colour bars sit in a column to the right of the matrix, which suits a wide screen. For a printed page, janusplot_style(legend_position = "bottom", label_srt = 0) puts the bars and the key under the matrix, so the cells take the full width, and show_glossary = FALSE leaves the explanation to the figure caption.

colour_by = "edf" is accepted for one release and mapped to "nonlinearity" with a deprecation message.

See also

janusplot_fit() for the object, janusplot_style() for the appearance settings, janusplot() for the one-call form.

Other smooth-associations: janusplot(), janusplot_compare(), janusplot_curves(), janusplot_direction(), janusplot_fit(), janusplot_pair(), janusplot_reference(), janusplot_style(), plot.janusplot_compare()

Examples

fit <- janusplot_fit(mtcars[, c("mpg", "hp", "wt")], engine = "gam")
plot(fit)


# Redrawing with another colour_by, annotations, group or display
# needs no refit; vignette("janusplot") shows each of them.
